A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same JE/AIS/RDS research work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–I support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original normalizing-constant estimates and sampling-quality results for modified Müller Brown and Gaussian-mixture targets in Table 1 and Appendix I, with generated samples in Figures 2–3.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments on both targets, including normalizing-constant estimates, MMD and Wasserstein-distance results, and sample visualizations in Table 1 and Appendix I.

M1.justification: Equations (10) and (14) and Algorithms 1–2 retain the same AIS and RDS procedures and estimators. Algorithm 2's expanded description identifies the same four nonparametric score-estimation options already discussed in v2.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same two-dimensional modified Müller Brown distribution and four-component Gaussian mixture. Appendix I retains their potentials, mixture weights, means, and covariances; no additional evaluation scenario appears.

E2.justification: Table 1 and Figures 2–3 retain TI, AIS, RDMC, RSDMC, ZODMC, and SNDMC for both targets. The retained PIS and CMCD discussions are theoretical, not additional empirical comparisons.

E3.justification: Appendix I.3 retains the metrics and experimental settings, including 50,000–60,000 oracle calls per sample, 60,000 AIS steps at step size 0.01, and RDS duration 5 with stopping time 0.005 and 50 time points. Added theoretical parameter guidance does not revise these experiments.

E4.justification: The mode-coverage case studies and sample visualizations in Appendix I and Figures 2–3 are unchanged. No ablation, sensitivity study, or robustness experiment is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report 1,024 rounds with 1,024 independent trajectories per round and retain mean±standard-deviation reporting in Table 1. The numerical-integration error reported for the Müller Brown ground truth also remains unchanged.

E6.justification: All Table 1 entries and the plotted samples in Figures 2–3 match. For example, Gaussian-mixture RDMC Z-hat/Z remains 1.0001±0.0850, and SNDMC Wasserstein distance remains 1.5494±0.6820. The reported rankings and mode-coverage findings are retained.

T1.justification: Appendix E.2 replaces v2's Gaussian-specific Fisher-divergence decay argument with a KL-dissipation derivation for a general reference distribution, asserting that total action equals initial KL divergence. It then recovers the unchanged Gaussian bound dβ+m² through log-Sobolev inequality. This is a localized proof extension; the headline JE/AIS bounds remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same contributions: action-based non-asymptotic JE/AIS guarantees without explicit isoperimetric assumptions, a geometric-interpolation limitation, and RDS-based estimation. The conclusion preserves these central claims.

C2.justification: Section 4 adds conditions for extending the AIS proof to other interpolation curves and compensatory drifts. Section 5 adds an explanation linking rapid mass transfer between separated modes to slow mixing, and Section 6 adds parallel samplers as a possible extension. Existing limitations are retained.

D1.justification: v3 adds an experimental-code access statement in Section 5, explicit AIS step-size scaling at the end of Appendix D, and TI intermediate-distribution and particle-count scalings in Appendix H.1. These supplement the documentation of existing procedures; Appendix I's experimental settings remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Havens et al. (2025) on adjoint sampling, Tawn et al. (2020) on tempering, and several parallel-sampling references. Research positioning otherwise remains stable. FEAT, cited under He et al. in v2 and Du et al. in v3, is the same work with updated bibliographic details.

P1.justification: Notation moves from Appendix A to the introduction, and the duplicate informal transport lemma becomes a reference to the retained appendix statement. Local explanations of Langevin dynamics and backward SDEs, cross-references, and acknowledgments are added, while the overall narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v3 extensively reformats the document with a narrower text area, conference headers, new title and heading styles, and shaded goal/theorem boxes. Figure 1 changes from a large centered display to a smaller panel surrounded by text; Table 1 and appendix figures are resized and reflowed without changing their scientific content.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2, the explicit parameter guidance in Appendices D and H.1, code-access statement, and clearer background explanations improve usability and reproducibility documentation. Appendix E.2 also provides a more informative action/KL derivation. These limited gains outweigh the reduced readability of the smaller Figure 1; the algorithms, headline bounds, and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
